subject: Dedicated sizing: GPU guardrail + soft-hold for CascadeAI close
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CascadeAI (CAS-4321) — quick availability check + request for soft-hold

Team —

We have CascadeAI verbally committing to a Dedicated capacity purchase (deal CAS-4321). Legal/procurement cadence looks like procurement will need ~2 weeks to return signed SOW/DocuSign; customer wants production onboarding July 1. High-level asks:

- Can we confirm fleet availability for a sustained Dedicated pool that approximates: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs for production + 4x for staging (sustained across 12 months)?
- Can ops place a 14–30 day soft-hold / guardrail on the relevant node pool to prevent reallocation during procurement?

Numbers are approximate; we can refine after your sizing notes. CascadeAI is sensitive to latency and plan to run mixed-precision with KV cache persistence. If we need a different SKU (A100 vs H100) we'll surface cost/latency tradeoffs to the AE and the customer.

I pulled the customer’s expected ramp: prod steady-state 300 RPS inference (avg seq len 512) and a small staging footprint for canaries.

Please respond with: snapshot of available capacity in target region, recommended buffer (%), and your preferred soft-hold mechanism (ledger tag / reservation id / ticket).

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CascadeAI (CAS-4321) — quick availability check + request for soft-hold

David / team —

Quick capacity snapshot for us-west-2:
- Pool: dedicated-prod-3 (H100 fleet): 24 GPUs total free (uncommitted).
- Pool: staging-tiling-1 (A100): 12 GPUs free.

Sizing note: To hit ~300 RPS at seq=512 with KV caching we estimate ~6–8 H100 equiv for steady-state. Given single-tenant overhead and patching windows, recommend 20% operational buffer => request 10 H100-equivalents in the reservation. For staging, request 4 A100 equiv.

Soft-hold options:
1) Ledger reservation (frontend tag + backend reservation id). We can create reservation RESV-9891 with a 30-day soft block that prevents autoscale reclaim.
2) Node-pool lock (more intrusive) — prevents any reassignments but requires ops exception.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with the pool inventory and projected fragmentation. If you want, we can create RESV-9891 now and mark it as 'soft' (not billed) pending contract signature; ops will release automatically if not confirmed by the hold expiry.

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_may25.xlsx

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-25T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CascadeAI (CAS-4321) — quick availability check + request for soft-hold

Ben — good snapshot. Couple of operational items to lock in: 

- Buffer: +20% sounds right; call it "sizing cushion" in the SOW so we can flex without immediate churn.
- SLA impact: if we reserve RESV-9891 for 30 days, we should attach a fallback routing policy to reduce risk (route to a compatible lower-cost model / cross-region burst) in case of unexpected capacity events.
- Onboarding: CS needs to be looped early — attaching the MOP/onboarding checklist so the AE can share expected timelines and runbook steps with the customer during procurement.

I can approve creating RESV-9891 as a soft-hold. Ops prefers a ledger reservation rather than a hard node lock — less friction for other customers and easier rollback. If AE confirms procurement timeline (signed SOW by 2 weeks), we flip the reservation to committed and bill.

Attachment: MOP_and_onboarding_checklist.pdf

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Dedicated Sales Operations
